notes: Correction to step 1: I added the optional external LED circuit that the tutorial lists (220 ohm resistor and red LED on pin 13). The task says to include it, and the earlier graph left pin 13 unwired.

External LED circuit: pin 13 goes through wire4 to the 220 ohm resistor, then to the LED anode. The LED cathode goes through wire5 to the GND pin next to pin 13, which I named GND.1. This follows the tutorial's text. No image shows it, so the breadboard columns 20-25 are my own choice.

The tutorial offers a potentiometer circuit or a photoresistor plus 10K resistor circuit. I built the potentiometer circuit, which the text describes in detail, and left out the photoresistor circuit.
Breadboard coordinates for the potentiometer are read from its image. The catalogue's 't' bank is rows a-e, the lower half in the picture. The 'b' bank is rows f-j, the upper half.

The potentiometer legs are at column 10 (GND, outer leg), column 12 (VCC, outer leg) and column 11 (SIG, middle leg, which points up to the far side of the centre gap). The text only says one outer pin goes to ground and the other to 5V, so I followed the image: black to the left leg and red to the right leg.
The yellow wire ends where the middle leg is drawn. A wire cannot share a hole with the leg, so I put the leg in 11b.g and the wire end in 11b.h, in the same strip.
The black ground wire goes to the second GND pin of the power header, which I named GND.2. Any Uno GND is the same node.
